# intutic_task_connection (Resource)

A task-management connection (`/api/v1/task-management/connections`): Jira Cloud, Linear or PagerDuty, which Intutic reads tickets and incidents through to attach task context to sessions. It never creates or updates them. The control plane tests the credentials with the provider and saves the connection only if they are accepted, so an apply with a token the provider refuses fails. The API never returns `api_token` or `account_email`, so they are kept in Terraform state as configured; protect the state accordingly. The API has no update: changing any argument replaces the connection (a new id). An imported connection has no `api_token` or `account_email` in state, so the first apply after an import replaces it with the configured values. Destroying it removes the connection and its token. Needs an OWNER or ADMIN key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Jira Cloud: a branch or commit naming PROJ-123 picks up that ticket's
# context. Jira signs an API token in as its account, so account_email is
# required. Changing any argument replaces the connection.
resource "intutic_task_connection" "jira" {
  task_provider = "jira"
  base_url      = "https://acme.atlassian.net"
  project_key   = "PROJ"
  account_email = "platform@acme.com"
  api_token     = var.jira_api_token
}

# Linear: project_key is the team key (eng-123 matches ENG).
resource "intutic_task_connection" "linear" {
  task_provider = "linear"
  base_url      = "https://api.linear.app"
  project_key   = "ENG"
  api_token     = var.linear_api_key
}

variable "jira_api_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "linear_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_token` (String, Sensitive) The provider API token: a Jira API token, a Linear API key or a PagerDuty REST API token. The API never returns it; it is kept in state as configured. Changing it replaces the connection.
- `base_url` (String) The provider's base URL, for example `https://acme.atlassian.net` for Jira Cloud. Changing it replaces the connection.
- `project_key` (String) The Jira project key, Linear team key or PagerDuty service key a ticket or incident is matched on. Changing it replaces the connection.
- `task_provider` (String) The task manager: one of `jira`, `linear`, `pagerduty` (the API's `provider`; `provider` is a Terraform meta-argument). Changing it replaces the connection.

### Optional

- `account_email` (String) Jira only, and required for Jira: the Atlassian account the API token belongs to (Jira Cloud signs a token in as that account). Not returned by the API. Changing it replaces the connection.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the connection was created (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) The connection id (`cc_…`).
- `status` (String) Always `connected`: the API saves a connection only once the provider accepts its credentials. A token revoked later still reads `connected`; `intutic tasks test` checks it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by connection id, as `intutic tasks list` shows it. The API never
# returns the token or the Jira account email, and has no update, so the first
# apply after an import replaces the connection with the configured values.
terraform import intutic_task_connection.jira cc_0123456789abcdef
```
